status: experimental interoperability profile; not production promoted
core_invariant: A request must remain inside a verified local grant and a pre-bound intent, and must remain safe in composition with prior actions sharing the same causal authority scope.
rationale: Transport sessions are not trusted security boundaries. Composition state follows a causal_scope_id so changing protocol, reconnecting, or splitting transport sessions cannot automatically erase the relevant authority history.

inputs.verified_grant: Cryptographically or otherwise independently verified before this semantic evaluator is called.
inputs.bound_intent: Application-bound narrowing context. Intent may reduce but never expand grant authority.
inputs.request: Exact principal, resource/audience, action, purpose, destination, policy digest, protocol and causal scope.
inputs.history: Prior admitted actions keyed to causal_scope_id rather than transport session.

normative_properties: identity/discovery/protocol metadata have no authority effect
resource or audience mismatch fails closed
protocol transitions do not reset causal composition history
individually admissible actions can still be denied when their composition is prohibited
composition restrictions are explicit and auditable rather than inferred by an LLM
absence of a verified grant or bound intent is not silently repaired by stronger identity evidence

rejected: treating protocol authentication as sufficient local effect authority

research_alignment.source: Bounded Agents / Agentic Principal Chain, arXiv:2608.15888
extended: composition state follows causal authority scope, not only a transport session, reducing session-splitting evasion
rejected: importing APC as a required Mesh runtime or authority vocabulary

retained: separate evidence characterization from deterministic policy
rejected: requiring ASP or any specific policy engine in the Mesh core

retained: multi-hop delegation as separate composable inputs
rejected: hard-coding OAuth as the Mesh authority substrate

retained: separation of identity, authorization, attestation, evidence and trust
rejected: collapsing trust into a universal scalar or reputation score

limitations: The semantic evaluator does not verify signatures or tokens itself.
Composition restrictions must be authored; unknown harmful combinations are not magically inferred.
Causal scope continuity must itself be integrity-bound by the calling authority path.
This profile does not claim standards conformance or production readiness.
